bibl.author: Anonymous
bibl.note:
Commentary following closely the Indian base text. It contains a light analysis of how the elements of the twelve links it together, and its treatment of philosophical matters is also quite light.
It does not have a colophon indicating the author and title, concluding instead with a completion statement indicating the text commented upon (slob dpon klu grub kyis mdzad pa'i ¦ rten cing 'brel par 'byung pa'i snyin po'i tshig le'ur byas pa || rdzogs s+h+yo ||)

bibl.note: Topical outline of Candrakīrti's (ID:3725) Bodhisattvayogācāracatuḥśatakaṭīkā (ID:5931), with lemmata indicated in interlinear notes in instance (ID:5134).

bibl.title: spyod 'jug gi bsdus don dang slob dpon zhi ba lha'i lo rgyus
སྤྱོད་འཇུག་གི་བསྡུས་དོན་དང་སློབ་དཔོན་ཞི་བ་ལྷའི་ལོ་རྒྱུས
bibl.author: Anonymous
bibl.note: In spite of the title suggested in an annotation on top of the first folio, this is not a topical outline of the Bodhicaryāvatāra (ID:3727). The text starts with announcing a discussion of the 5 "elements for explaining the treatise." The first (the author) covers 3 folios in (ID:5142), dealing with Śāntideva's (ID:3743) life, organized around seven specific deeds he performed and for each of which he received a different name. The second element (the place of composition), the third (the title), the fourth (the purpose), and the fifth (the homage (?)), are all dealt with on the last folio side.

bibl.title: gnyis su med pa'i shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i gdams pa don brgyad du bsdus nas rgyas par bshad pa
གཉིས་སུ་མེད་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་གདམས་པ་དོན་བརྒྱད་དུ་བསྡུས་ནས་རྒྱས་པར་བཤད་པ
jo bo rje'i gdams pa
gnyis med shes rab pha rol du phyin pa zab mo lam gyi gdams pa
bibl.author: Anonymous
bibl.note:
The title suggests a report of Atiśa's (ID:3745) teaching on the Perfection of wisdom. The text is divided in eight sections. In (ID:5174), the portion explaining the eight topics covers fol. 37a1-61b4, ending with "rdzogs so" and is followed, up to 62b4, by a summarized explanation (don brgyad du bstan pa'i gdam ngag la spyir bsdus don gyi tshul du rnam par bshad pa) which starts with "da ni" and ends with "jo bo rje'i gdams pa rdzogs s+h+hyo."
The contents of the first third of the text is more tied to Madhyamaka than Perfection of wisdom, and includes digressions about the perspectives of the "hearers" (nyan thos), "idealists" (sems tsam), and Madhyamaka (dbu ma) and a refutation of idealism. The author uses tools and vocabulary of epistemology (e.g., gnod pa'i tshad ma, lhan cig mi gnas pa'i 'gal ba), but refutes perception and inference being instances of valid cognition (fol. 42). New sections start with the expression "da ni."
The views of other scholars, who are not named, are mentioned about 10 times (often with the expression "kha cig dag di ltar sems ste). The expression "zhe na" is used for questions to provide answers to rather than hypothetical objections.

bibl.title: tshig le'ur byas pa sum brgyar pa'i don gsal bar byed
ཚིག་ལེའུར་བྱས་པ་སུམ་བརྒྱར་པའི་དོན་གསལ་བར་བྱེད

bibl.note: This commentary is very similar to the dGe tshul gyi tshig le'ur byas pa sum brgya pa'i tshig don rab tu 'byed pa (ID:5524) by Dharma singha (who could be Phya pa Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3831)). This suggests the author could be the same, or the author of the present work might be a student of the author of (ID:5524).

bibl.title: 'dul ba mdo'i dgos 'brel
འདུལ་བ་མདོའི་དགོས་འབྲེལ
bibl.author: Anonymous
bibl.note:
This untitled and anonymous text (possibly incomplete) essentially discusses the "purpose and connection" (dgos 'brel) of a treatise (hence the editorial title). It is only on fol. 5a in (ID:5275) that it reveals itself to be about monastic discipline, identifying the topic of the treatise as "chos 'di pa dag gi tshul khrims." The treatise under consideration is likely the Vinayasūtra (ID:6821), which has the expression "tshul khrims" in its initial verse. The text makes several references to Dharmamitra, the author of the Vinayasūtraṭīkā (ID:8404).
The frequent use of thal...phyir arguments and reference to the Pramāṇavārttika (ID:3772) suggest a date of composition in the 13th c. or beyond. The discussion of dgos 'brel has close parallels to the one found in the Tik chen lung don rnam gzigs (ID:5870) by Chu mig pa Seng ge dpal (ID:4018).

The author supports the view of the prāsaṅgika orientation and of the "great Madhyamaka" (dbu ma chen po). The text covers basic notions such as the types of valid cognition, the theory of definition, the two truths. Arguments are frequently presented in the chos can-te-phyir and chos can-thal-phyir format. It includes numerous citations of Indian works.

bibl.author: Anonymous
bibl.note:
The author claims to follow the tradition of Maitripa, but aside from a couple of mentions of this name, not a lot is found to substantiate this. The work shows strong influences of the Abhisamayālaṅkāra commentarial tradition according to Haribhadra (ID:3712). Unlike other doxographies, this is initially geared towards meditation, but in a philosophically informed way. It gradually gets more scholastic in content and style (using, in particular, the pronoun "khyod" in argumentation).
Quotes an unidentified "slob dpon 'gog pa seng ge" (ID:7352).

bibl.note: Incomplete commentary on the Abhisamayālaṃkāra­ (ID:3706). Features abundant use of "chos can...thal/te...phyir" arguments, including also the use of the pronoun "khyod" as a variable. Although the manuscript was grouped with works by rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) in [XCKNA9JH], rNgog Blo ldan shes rab does not appear to have been the author. In particular, the above-mentioned features are not found in other works of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab. Discussed in [DQZ4IIQZ]: 59 (170) and 76-78 (151-153).
